gap: No result ChatGPT got states that StorageReview measured only 920 Wh from the ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro (about 63% of its 1,451 Wh rating, with the unit shutting off at 22% shown), against the 1,910 Wh StorageReview measured from the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2.
standout_why: Compared against: StormWatts (cited, read 2026-11-17), which says 'We have not tested these products hands-on' and lists only rated Wh for its 24 kits, plus one owner solar test on a Jackery 2000 Plus that is not in the kit list. Also Powersized /best/solar-generator/, which carries only two measurements, both from OutdoorGearLab: the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 at 1,710 Wh and the BLUETTI AC180 at 950 Wh. ChatGPT's own answer took 1,710 Wh for the Jackery and StorageReview's 1,910 Wh for the Elite 200 V2 from our own page. None of these has a measured figure for any ALLPOWERS station, and none has the Anker C1000 Gen 2 at 907 Wh or its roughly 17 W no-load drain. Some pages could not be checked: Popular Mechanics (cited) blocked the fetcher, and theoutageready, lightsonlabs and solargenadvisor failed on a TLS certificate error. The score is 2, not 3, because those pages are unverified.
decides: The pick has to ship now, and the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 kits are pre-orders dispatching Nov 26, 2026, so the ALLPOWERS kits that ship now are the obvious stand-ins. On rated Wh the S2000 Pro + SP037 400 W kit looks cheap: $917.93 link price / 1,451 Wh = $0.63 per rated Wh. Using StorageReview's 920 Wh it is about $1.00 per usable Wh. The Elite 200 V2 + 2x200 W kit works out to about $0.75 per usable Wh ($1,424.05 / 1,910) and the Elite 200 V2 + 200 W kit to about $0.60 ($1,139.05 / 1,910). The Solar Lab also reports the S2000 Pro shutting off at 55% battery under a 2,250 W load. The page should not make the S2000 Pro kit the ships-now pick on price per Wh. Name the Elite 200 V2 kit as the better value for a shopper who can wait until Nov 26. The R2500 V2 and R3500 kits, which also ship now, have no named lab measurement, so the page has to label them as rated only.

findings.label: Measured AC discharge capacity
findings.source_title: ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro Portable Power Station Review – StorageReview
findings.note: StorageReview Consumer Desk, April 7, 2023. 350 W load. 'the unit powered off with 22 percent remaining.' The article gives the rating as 1,500 Wh, while our kit table uses 1,451 Wh: 920/1,451 = 63%, 920/1,500 = 61%. A full AC recharge took 1,090 Wh. This was a 2023 unit, so firmware may have changed since.

findings.label: High-load cutoff
findings.value: shut off at 55% battery under a 2,250 W load
findings.source_title: AllPowers S2000 Pro Review: Can AllPowers Redeem Itself? – The Solar Lab
findings.note: The Solar Lab: 'we ran a 2,250-watt load—well below its advertised maximum limit' and the unit 'shut off at 55% battery.' It calls the efficiency 'trash' but gives no Wh figure. No date or author was shown on the page.

findings.label: Measured usable capacity, AC
findings.value: 1,123 Wh at 200 W AC; 1,133 Wh at 1,200 W AC
findings.source_title: Test: ALLPOWERS S2000, große, gute und günstige Powerstation – Techtest
findings.note: Michael Barton, Techtest, June 17, 2023. That is 75–76% of 1,500 Wh rated. On DC it measured 1,395.4 Wh (12 V/5 A) and 1,345.8 Wh (USB-C 20 V/5 A). AC charging efficiency was 64–79%. This is the station in our S2000 + SF200/SP037 kits. The test used the EU 230 V model.

findings.label: Measured discharge and recharge energy
findings.source_title: Portable Power Meets Lab-Grade Reliability: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Review – StorageReview
findings.note: Dylan Dougherty, StorageReview, April 25, 2025. UPS test in a home-lab rack with the load at 986 W–1.1 kW. 1,910/2,073.6 = 92% of rated. 1,910/2,440 = 78% round trip (my arithmetic). Our own page already carries this figure.

findings.label: Measured solar input
findings.value: 520–550 W at start, 600 W peak, 245 W under cloud
findings.source_title: Bluetti Elite 200 V2 Test & Review – CleanTechnica
findings.note: Z. S., CleanTechnica, July 7, 2025. The excerpt does not name the panel set. That is more panel wattage than the 200 W or 2x200 W kits include, so it shows what the station can take in, not what those kits will deliver.

findings.label: Measured energy output
findings.value: 1,710 Wh (spec table); the text says 1,740 Wh
findings.note: Chris McNamara with Kenji Mowrey, OutdoorGearLab, November 3, 2025. Measured in real-world use (string lights, laptop, Starlink, induction stovetop), not on a bench load. 84% of 2,042 Wh. Powersized and our page already carry this figure.

findings.label: Measured energy delivered
findings.note: Kenji Mowrey, OutdoorGearLab, January 13, 2026. Light-bar test jig at 80% load until fully drained. 18% below the 1,152 Wh rating. Powersized already carries this figure. Our AC180 + 2x200 W kit at $1,170.40 link price works out to $1.23 per measured Wh.

findings.label: Measured usable capacity and no-load drain
findings.value: 907 Wh at 1 kW; about 17 W idle with the inverter on
findings.source_title: Record-Breaking Charge Speed: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 Power Station Review – The Technology Man
findings.note: Gidon, The Technology Man, November 4, 2025. Constant 1 kW resistive heater on an energy-monitoring plug: just over 54 minutes, 907 Wh, which is 89% of 1,024 Wh. With no load the battery fell from 100% to 80% in 12 hours, which the author puts at about 17 W. Two 200 W Renogy panels in parallel gave about 170 W.

unsourced: No named lab or reviewer measurement for the ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 (1,920 Wh) or R3500 (3,168 Wh). The only R3500 figure found was Exspenditure's 'about 3,200 Wh', which it measures against 3,500 Wh in one table and 3,168 Wh in another, so it is not usable. The ALLPOWERS 86% figure is the maker's planning number, not a measurement.

No measured usable Wh for the BLUETTI Pioneer Na (900 Wh sodium-ion). The cold-weather figure of 80% at -25 °C reported by ESS News, PopSci and pv-magazine looks like a maker claim; no named test reports it.
No measured usable Wh for the plain EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max. The Technology Man's 1,898 Wh at 2 kW is for the DELTA 3 Max Plus, a different model. Backup Power Hub's 1,741 Wh is an 85% estimate.
Backup Power Hub's 2,065 Wh at 200 W for the Elite 200 V2 was seen only in a search snippet and the page was not opened. It is left out.
OutdoorGearLab's 890 Wh and 87% efficiency, and CHIP's 839 Wh, for the Anker C1000 Gen 2 were seen only in search summaries and the pages were not opened. They are left out.
No measured solar input with the kit's own bundled panels for any kit in the budget.

Rival pages that could not be read to confirm they lack these figures: popularmechanics.com best-portable-power-stations (cited; fetch blocked), theoutageready.com, lightsonlabs.com, solargenadvisor.com (TLS certificate errors), solargenreview.com and gearjunkie.com (not opened, to stay within the call budget). Our own dealectric.com pages also failed on TLS; what they carry was inferred from ChatGPT's answer.
